MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  APRIL 14, 2025
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 4:46 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne  Riggins;  and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated Litigation

ROLL CALL

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne  Riggins;  and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  Jerry Vandermuelen, Fire Safety Liason

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Meril May led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 4:45 p.m., after which

  the Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recommended Action: 1) Authorize the Mayor to sign the National
  Wildlife Federation Mayors’ Monarch Pledge, renewing the City’s
  commitment to help save the monarch butterfly; and 2) Direct staff to
  implement measures to meet the commitments of the Mayors’ Monarch

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded
  a motion to: 1) Authorize the Mayor to sign the National Wildlife
  Federation Mayors’ Monarch Pledge, renewing the City’s commitment to
  help save the monarch butterfly; and 2) Direct staff to implement measures
  to meet the commitments of the Mayors’ Monarch Pledge in support of
  monarch and pollinator conservation in the Malibu community. The motion
  carried unanimously.

  Malibu Garbage Disposal District (MGDD), increase the compensation by

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded

  carried unanimously.

  Purchase of Los Angeles Regional Interoperable Communications System

  Recommended Action: Authorize the purchase of approved dual-band

ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  Proclamation Declaring April 20-27, 2025 National Volunteer Week

  Councilmember Conrad left the dais at 6:38 p.m.

  Mayor Stewart presented the proclamation to Public Safety Director Duefras and
  members of the Community Emergency Response Team (CERT_, Arson Watch
  and Volunteers on Patrol (VOP).

  Councilmember Conrad returned to the dais at 6:40 p.m.

  Public Safety Director Duefias discussed the contributions and accomplishments of
  the City’s volunteers.

  Presentation of City Tile to Graeme Clifford for his service as an Ex-Officio
  Commissioner

  Mayor Stewart presented the tile to Graeme Clifford.

  Graeme Clifford thanked the Council for the recognition and stated he intended to
  return to the City after being displaced by the flre.

  Presentation of City Tile to Suzanne Guldimann for her service on the Parks and
  Recreation Commission

  Mayor Stewart presented the tile to Suzanne Guldimann.

  Suzanne Guldimann thanked the Council for the recognition and stated she would
  continue volunteering in the community.

  Community Lands Update

  Acting Assistant City Manager Brown presented an update on the Community
  Lands project. She announced a Malibu Arts Commission meeting on April 22,
   Malibu City Council

  2025 at the La Paz site, and there would be additional updates on the performing
  arts center in late early June.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Scott Dittrich, Public Works Commission, discussed the PCH Master Plan and
  expressed his personal concerns regarding the plans for the east end of PCH.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Mr. Dittrich clarified that he was
  expressing his personal opinions.

  Acting City Manager Toney provided an update on fire rebuild statistics, including
  applications submitted and approved and public records requests. He discussed use
  of the lot at 4000 Malibu Canyon Road for staging during the Palisades Fire and
  explained that the City issued an Emergency Coastal Development Permit (ECDP)
  for the requiring the lot to be restored to its prior state. He announced that the right
  of entry form deadline was tomorrow. He announced upcoming fire recovery
  community meetings, PCH Mast Plan meeting, volunteer recognition reception,
  City Council work sessions, Malibu Association of Realtors event, and the City
  Council budget workshop.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, City Clerk Pettijohn and Acting City
  Manager Toney discussed public records request for flre rebuilds and how records
  requests are tracked and processed.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Acting City Manager Toney discussed
  the issuance of the ECDP for 4000 Malibu Canyon and confirmed the City had
  recent records of the state of the property for remediation.

  In response to Councilmember Conrad, Acting City Manager Toney confirmed the
  budget workshop would held be with the full Council.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, presented the
  March 2025 crime report. He provided an update on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH)
  access and shared an announcement from Governor Newsom on additional shifts
  for debris removal and plans to reopen PCH. He discussed changes to the route for
  debris removal trucks. He announced that the National Guard was tentatively
  scheduled to demobilize April 30, 2025. He stated the opt-in/opt-out deadline for
  the debris removal program was April 30, 2025. He stated the Beach Team would
  start operating Memorial Day weekend.

ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Debra Oser, Pegasus Transportation, discussed her business’s transportation and
  shuttle services and offered their services to the City.

Tim Pera, Mountains Recreation Conservation Authority Ranger, presented the
Coastal Ranger Report for February and March, including statistics on citations
issued. He stated coastal parks were closed due to the recent fires but maintenance
continues. He stated soastal access areas closed until further notice per the
Governor’s Executive Order. He stated extended patrols were implemented due to
closures.

In response to Councilmember Silverstein and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Ranger
Pera discussed the trash collected as part of maintenance activities.

Lance Walker discussed his qualifications professional experience as an arborist in
the area. He stated he wanted to help save trees.

Ed Niles was not present at the time of the hearing.

Arno Koch discussed a Rebuild Czar position and the City Council work session
where this topic was discussed. He stated the public had provided proposals for the
role of the Rebuild Czar.

Fred Wicks deferred time to Peter Stricker.

Peter Stricker, Seawell, discussed water desalination and his company’s proposal
for offshore desalination buoys to provide additional water supply.

In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, and
Councilmember Conrad discussed desalination.

Mikke Pierson stated he would speak on Item No. 7.B.

Sam Boyer deferred time to Yvonne Green.

Yvonne Green, 99 High Tide, discussed impacts of the Palisades Fire on her
business and others. She requested the Council adopt an urgency ordinance for an
eviction moratorium and grants.

Jim Rogers stated his house was destroyed in the Palisades Fire and he intended to
rebuild like-for-like. He discussed discrepancies between the number of fixtures
permitted at his house and the incomplete permitting records for his property. He
discussed how reopening PCH impacts rebuilding.

Salwa Wahba discussed the work session last Thursday and her family’s rebuilding
experience. She discussed the importance of making quick decisions.

Lea Johnson deferred time to Scott Dittrich.

Scott Dittrich discussed rebuilding and owners who were selling their property

rather than rebuilding. He encouraged the Councilmembers to Visit the rebuild sites
and inspect the slabs. He discussed requirements for new foundations and
requested the Council allow different requirements for rebuilds.

Patt Healy presented the Council with monarch butterfly trading cards.

Charlotte Frieze introduced the artist who designed the trading cards.

Dean Wenner recommended additional traffic enforcement in the PCH construction
zone. He discussed the delayed release of geology guidelines for fire rebuilds. He
discussed requirement for beachfront properties to install a new onsite wastewater
treatment system (OWTS).

Lynn Dornhelm discussed challenges for f1re rebuilds in Carbon Canyon due to
insufficient fire flow.

In response to Ms. Dornhelm, Acting Assistant City Manager Brown and
Environmental Sustainability Director Bundy explained the fire flow issue and
recommended scheduling the topic for a work session.

Councilmember Silverstein stated he had heard there was miscommunication and
some residents believed the fire flow issue would be discussed tonight.

Mayor Stewart apologized for the confusion.

Ms. Dornhelm stated the fire flow issue had been a problem since 1994.

Michael Shane and Meril May deferred time to Kimberly Carr.

Kimberly Carr discussed ways to improve safety on PCH including renaming the
road, roundabouts, and a road zipper to switch the direction of lanes.

Jimmy Petulla expressed frustration with the City and with the fees for rebuild
permits. He discussed impacts on his business from the PCH road closure.

David Illulian discussed his house that was destroyed in the 1993 fire and his efforts
to rebuild.

In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Principal Planner Eaton clarified how
water tanks could be permitted as part of a fire rebuild. Environmental
Sustainability Director Bundy discussed fire flow requirements.

Councilmember Conrad left the dais at 8:22 p.m.

Jefferson Wagner encouraged the public to work through the challenging rebuilding
process. He discussed issues getting PCH passes for his employees.

ITEM 7  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Consideration of a Broad, Franklin and Palisades Fire Rebuild Fee Waiver Program
  Recommended Action: Provide direction to staff regarding a fee waiver program
  for the Broad, Franklin and Palisades fire rebuilds.

  Councilmember Silverstein recused himself and left the dais at 10:04 p.m.

  Interim Planning Director Tamuri presented the staff report.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Dean Wenner, Jo Drummond, and Howard Rudzki

  Kevin Keegan declined the opportunity to speak.

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to waive fees similar
  to Woolsey Fire Fee Waiver Program, with the following provisions: 1) waive all
  fees for like-for-like plus 10%, 2) only waive fees for the owners at the time of the
  f1re and their heirs, 3) only waive fees for individuals or revocable trusts, 4) June
  2028 deadline.

  Councilmember Conrad left the dais at 10:30 p.m.

  Councilmember Silverstein retumed to the dais at 10:31 p.m.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Silverstein second a motion

  B.  Consideration and Direction Regarding Business Assistance Efforts Post Palisades
  Fire
  Recommended Action: 1) Receive a Presentation on Business Impact Survey
  results conducted in response to Palisades Fire and related disruptions; 2) Provide
  Direction on establishment of City of Malibu Small Business Micro Grant
  Assistance Program; 3) Provide directions on implementing a business promotion
  campaign to reaffirm that Malibu Businesses are open and accessible; and 4)
  Provide Direction on whether to implement or pause 2025 Minimum Wage Increase
  in Malibu.

  Acting Assistant City Manager Brown presented the staff report.

  Councilmember Conrad returned to the dais at 10:33 p.m.

  Acting Assistant City Manager Brown continued the staff report.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Don Schmitz, Michel Shane, Kevin Keegan, Jo Drummond, Mikke
  Pierson, Yvonne Green, Rafi Anteby, Howard Rudzki

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to 1) discuss a business promotion
  campaign with the Chamber of Commerce, and 2) bring back a proposal from a
  m1cro-grant program.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to suspend the
  minimum wage increase for one year.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back at a regular meeting options
  for streamlining Temporary Use Permits and relax signage regulations to support
